entries.title: 1. Land Banks — the single biggest hidden source
entries.summary: ## 1. Land Banks — the single biggest hidden source **Why hidden:** Most investors don't know land banks exist. Most general-purpose aggregators don't index them. They handle property that *already failed* tax foreclosure and went to the municipality.

entries.title: 1. Land Banks — the single biggest hidden source
entries.summary: **Pattern:** Most land bank sites have either (a) a tabular search form, or (b) a CSV/JSON export. Cleveland's site is at `clevelandohio.gov` and has searchable inventory. Detroit's `buildingdetroit.org` is a custom React app with API behind it. ---

entries.title: 2. Vacant Property Registries (1,900+ ordinances)
entries.summary: ## 2. Vacant Property Registries (1,900+ ordinances) **Why hidden:** Local. No national index. Each city has its own ordinance, fee structure, and database. **What they are:** Cities require owners of vacant properties to register, often paying escalating annual fees.

entries.title: 3. Code Violations / Building Permits (city open data)
entries.summary: ## 3. Code Violations / Building Permits (city open data) **Why hidden:** These are open data portals that exist in most major US cities. Most investors don't know to check them, and they're not in any major aggregator (yet).

entries.title: 4. Pre-Foreclosure Filings (NOD, Lis Pendens) — the canonical off-market lead
entries.summary: ## 4. Pre-Foreclosure Filings (NOD, Lis Pendens) — the canonical off-market lead **Why hidden (relatively):** Most investors use paid aggregators (ATTOM, PropStream) because going to 3,142 county recorders individually is impractical. But the data IS public.

entries.title: 5. Tax Delinquency Lists (county treasurers, annual)
entries.summary: ## 5. Tax Delinquency Lists (county treasurers, annual) **Why hidden:** Updated annually. Most investors miss them. Free but require going to each county treasurer's website. **What they are:** Properties with unpaid property taxes.

entries.title: 6. Probate / Estate Filings (county court records)
entries.summary: ## 6. Probate / Estate Filings (county court records) **Why hidden:** County courthouse records. Most online, some still paper-only. **What they are:** When someone dies owning real estate, the heirs must go through probate. Often the heirs want to sell.

entries.title: 8. HOA Foreclosure (super-lien states)
entries.summary: ## 8. HOA Foreclosure (super-lien states) **Why hidden:** Separate from mortgage foreclosure. HOA has its own lien that can foreclose even if the mortgage is current.
